verdicts.question: What type of roof is present at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 6, 9, 10 and the roof-top view/render (page 17) all show a bare, flat concrete (RCC) terrace with parapet walls on all sides and no visible tiles or sheet metal.
verdicts.rationale: Roof surface is unambiguously a flat poured-concrete slab consistent with 'RCC Flat Roof'.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstructions on the roof that could affect the solar installation?
verdicts.designer_notes: The skylights and west side headroom and east side parapet wall are the obstructions that could affect the solar installation
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 6 roof photo shows a skylight/glass hatch on the terrace; page 17-18 top-view/3D renders show a raised headroom room on the west side of the array; and the Shadow Analysis pages (19-21) explicitly draw shaded zones on the panels from the 'east-side parapet wall' (9-11am), 'west-side parapet wall' (3-4:30pm) and 'west-side headroom' (2-4:30pm, affecting the first 1-2 rows).
verdicts.rationale: The designer's own notes list skylights, west headroom, and east parapet wall as obstructions, and the shadow-analysis diagrams in the same document confirm all three actually cast shadows on the panel array at various times of year. This directly contradicts the multiple-choice answer of 'No' obstructions.

verdicts.question: What is the angle of the panels? (in degrees)
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 18-19 show a 3D ballast-structure render with front leg height 0.43m and rear leg height 1.18m over the module run; no photo has a protractor/angle overlay, and these are CAD renders of the proposed structure rather than as-built site photos.
verdicts.rationale: The render's leg-height difference (0.75m) suggests a tilt somewhat steeper than 10° depending on exact base spacing, but since this is a design mock-up (not a measured site photo) the angle cannot be confirmed or refuted with confidence.

verdicts.question: On how many roofs at the site are we installing solar?

verdicts.question: What type of mounting structure is planned?

verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target — the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 10-12 show a DC cable (red) + DC earthing cable (dark green) route drawn along the roof parapet and down a building corner to a junction near the equipment room. Pages 13-14 show a separate AC/DC/LA earthing route drawn through an existing conduit-pipe shaft down to earth pits (pages 16-17). Page 15 shows the Inverter/ACDB/DCDB/Battery wiring diagram, and page 22 shows the actual (already-installed) AC cable from inverter location to the main meter. However, the colored lines on pages 10-17 are route-overlay markups on an as-yet-uncabled site (pre-installation survey), not photos of physically installed and secured cable/conduit.
verdicts.rationale: The proposed routing is logically continuous and consistent with the legend (panel array -> parapet/corner run -> equipment room -> earth pits / main meter) with no obvious orphan segments or color/size mismatches in the diagrams. However, most of these are pre-installation overlay markups on bare surfaces rather than photos of actual installed cable, conduit, or cable-ties, so physical continuity and clipping/dressing cannot be confirmed from these images alone (the one exception, page 22, does show real already-run cable).
